thumbnail_prompt:
TWO images, IDENTICAL in every respect except WHO is in the frame. Same Pichwai/Kangra miniature style, same aged-parchment palette, same ornate border, same first-light morning landscape, same text banner at ~35% of frame reading START CLEAR with a second tier 'Sitar · Raga Ahir Bhairav'.

ARM A (VIEWER): a person waking and stretching in bed at first light, eyes just opening, unhurried. A sitar rests at the FRAME EDGE, not being played, not the subject.

ARM B (PERFORMER): a musician seated cross-legged PLAYING the sitar as the subject of the frame. No sleeping/waking figure.

Everything else pixel-comparable. The person is the only difference.
thumbnail_ab_note: ⭐⭐ THE WEEK'S TEST — first true IMAGE-COMPOSITION A/B on the channel. Of 68 A/B rows on record: 33 varied title+thumb together (unattributable), 16 title-only, 17 thumb-TEXT-only, and exactly ONE varied the image alone. The viewer-vs-performer gap (6.11% vs 3.03%) is the largest effect in §7b but it is a CROSS-SECTION confounded by lane, era and title — never an experiment. This isolates it. Read per-arm CTR at d7. If A wins, it is the biggest lever on the channel and every future thumbnail changes.
suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no humming — flowing Indian classical sitar in Raga Ahir Bhairav, bright plucked tone with gentle sustain, light tabla, 78 BPM, seamless loop.
suno_prompt_note: Short one-liner (~170 chars). MORNING-CLARITY lane: BPM at 78 (clarity band 70-80), energy retained — this is not a calm lane. 'flowing' not 'slow' (the word 'slow' makes Suno drag; reserved for sleep/deep-rest). Tabla IS correct here — the tabla rule is Sitar-only. Ahir Bhairav is the canonical morning raga and is unused in any live title. Binaural: alpha 10 Hz at -20dB.
